problem:
Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ given below. Find $det(A)-det({B}^{T}).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{2} & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2.5 & 0.21 \\ 0 & 2 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{2} & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}|=(-1)\cdot (-1)\cdot 2=2 \\ det(B) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2.5 & 0.21 \\ 0 & 2 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|=1\cdot 2\cdot (-3)=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Also, $det({B}^{T})=det(B)=-6.$ 

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(A)-det({B}^{T})=2-(-6)=8.
$$
